title: Quick check: Functional State Updates

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Functional State Updates”?
options: The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Updater functions should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
questions.answer_key: Updater functions should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Functional State Updates: Updater functions should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Updater functions?
options: Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
questions.answer_key: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Functional State Updates: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Functional State Updates” complete?
options: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Functional State Updates: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
